PullRequest.Title: sessions: add cloud automations to the composer dialog
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

Wave 4 of the cloud automations stack, targeting `bevillal/cloud-automations-routing` (#339419), not `main`. Adds the cloud create/edit dialog experience and workspace pickers on top of the wave 3 routing. Everything stays behind `chat.automations.cloud.enabled` (default off) and the parent Automations / AI-disabled gates.

**Choosing a cloud target**
- The workspace picker offers **Work in GitHub**. It reuses the New Chat repository search, shows only private repositories, and accepts a pasted repository URL. Picking a repository selects Cloud and keeps a matching local checkout as the displayed workspace.
- Local folders backed by an eligible private GitHub repository can choose Cloud directly from the session type picker. Other supported agents remain selectable; the execution provider is independent of the displayed workspace.
- Repository eligibility is checked per selected folder, at most 5 checks at a time, and cached until refresh or account change. Known public repositories hide Cloud for new automations, and a draft on Cloud falls back to Copilot when it switches to a public repository. Network failures never silently switch providers, and writes still revalidate on the server.
- When editing an existing cloud automation, the workspace picker is disabled because the repository and provider can't change; duplicating is the path to a new target.

**Form**
- Order is Target, Prompt (with the cloud model picker), Tools, then Schedule. There's no Enabled checkbox; editing preserves enabled state, and cards remain the place to enable or disable.
- **Tools** section: "Select which tools the agent can use. Built-in tools are always available." plus a **Configure allowed tools** button. It opens the shared quick tree picker, populated from the Mission Control tool catalog (`GET /agents/automations/tools`) with the server's groups, names, and descriptions. The catalog is loaded on demand, cached per account session, and shows loading, error, and Retry states without blocking the dialog.
  - New automations start with every catalog tool selected, and saving waits for the catalog if needed.
  - Saved tool IDs outside the catalog are shown under **Other Saved Tools** and preserved.
  - If GitHub didn't report saved tools on edit, they're left untouched.
- Schedules are shown and edited in local time and saved as GitHub's fixed UTC schedule; minutes off GitHub's quarter-hour grid are blocked with an inline message.
- With Cloud selected, a note beside Create reads "Runs even when your computer is off, triggered on a schedule."
- Escape inside the dialog now closes quick inputs (including the repository search) instead of being swallowed.

**Shared changes (minimal)**
- `IAutomationProviderConfiguration` and `IAutomationWorkspaceTarget` describe provider-owned dialog configuration and checked targets.
- `RepositoryPicker` takes an optional placeholder.
- `getGitHubRepositoryId` moved to `githubUrls.ts` so both pickers share it.
- `_findRelatedLocalWorkspace` is protected so the automation picker can reuse matching.
- New pure `automationScheduleToLocal`/`ToUTC` helpers.

## Scope and deferred work

Cards, run history/navigation, and native-session adoption are left for later waves. Repository discovery is limited to the user's known/recent private repositories; no account-wide scan. No changes to the API client contracts introduced in wave 1–3.

Open questions for the tool catalog: whether it includes the legacy IDs (`read`, `edit`, `bash`, `github/*`) is unverified, and new automations rely on built-in tools being always available server-side.

## How to test

1. Enable `chat.automations.cloud.enabled`, sign in to GitHub.com, open the Agents window and go to Automations.
2. **New Automation**: pick **Work in GitHub** → search for a private repo; Cloud is selected. Switch the folder to a public repo: Cloud disappears from the session type picker and the draft falls back to Copilot.
3. With Cloud selected, open **Configure allowed tools**, check the groups from the server, toggle a few, press Enter; Escape cancels without closing the dialog.
4. Pick a local time, create, and confirm the definition on GitHub has the matching UTC trigger. Reopen it: local time shows, the workspace picker is disabled, and enabled state is unchanged after saving.
5. With the feature off, or with a local agent selected, the dialog is unchanged.

## Validation

At head `65ad8fc1d28` (single commit on wave 3 at `fbb266ac94c`):

- `npx tsc --project src/tsconfig.json --noEmit --skipLibCheck`: passed.
- `node test/unit/browser/index.js --browser chromium --runGlob '**/{automationDialog,automationsView,cloudAutomationStore,githubCloudAutomationStore,copilotChatSessionsProvider,sessionTypePicker,sessionWorkspacePicker,repositoryPicker,schedule,automations.contribution}.test.js'`: **651 passed**.
- `scripts\test.bat --runGlob` (same glob, Electron): **648 passed, 4 pending**.
- ESLint on changed TypeScript files, Stylelint on `automationDialog.css`, `npm run valid-layers-check`, and commit hygiene hooks: passed.

Earlier in the branch, live validation in Code OSS against GitHub created two temporary disabled automations in a private repo to verify local-to-UTC conversion (09:45 PDT → 16:45 UTC; Sunday 23:45 PDT → Monday 06:45 UTC), then deleted them. That was before the move to the Mission Control base. **The Mission Control tool catalog and the rebased dialog have not yet been validated end to end against the live service.**

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The call path is direct: renderForm calls setCloudConfiguration, its autorun executes synchronously, and each uncached getWorkspaceTarget queues client.query.getRepository. The shared picker caps the default unified list at 10 rows and the new store caps concurrency at five, so the exact common-case burst is bounded but real; only the number of users with a full GitHub recent list and network duration are uncertain.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: One REST request per uncached GitHub recent-workspace row: up to 10 with the default unified picker, and potentially more when the legacy uncapped picker setting is used; five execute concurrently and refresh/account invalidation causes the burst to recur.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: excessive network I/O and avoidable contention for user-requested cloud data
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this diff, constructing the automation dialog did not install an eligibility observer or perform per-row repository visibility requests; workspace-picker rows were built locally and no GitHub metadata calls occurred merely because the dialog opened.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Constructing any automation dialog with cloud configuration now enumerates all recent GitHub workspace rows and starts an eligibility lookup for each one, even while the workspace picker remains closed.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT lines 2182-2188 add an autorun in setCloudConfiguration that immediately calls super._buildItems() and invokes getWorkspaceTarget(...).read(reader) for every GitHub row; renderForm calls setCloudConfiguration during dialog construction at RIGHT line 1264, before the workspace picker is opened.
Findings.Title: Defer per-repository eligibility reads until the picker opens
Findings.Impact: Opening the create/edit composer can launch up to ten unnecessary GitHub REST requests (five concurrently) before the user opens the workspace picker or chooses Cloud. On constrained connections these interactive-priority calls consume bandwidth/rate limit and compete with automation refresh and the tool-catalog request, slowing the cloud options the user actually uses.
Findings.Evidence: AutomationsWorkspacePicker.setCloudConfiguration loops over super._buildItems() and reads every GitHub target. CloudAutomationStore.configuration delegates each read to GitHubCloudAutomationStore.getWorkspaceTarget; on a cache miss that method queues a client.query.getRepository REST request. Repository reads use interactive priority. The default unified picker exposes up to 10 recent rows, while targetEligibilityLimiter permits five simultaneous requests. None of these row checks is needed to render the closed picker.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep the selected workspace eligibility read needed for session-type validation, but defer enumeration/checking of other rows until showPicker (and the existing mobile readiness path) actually opens the workspace picker; cancel or stop observing row checks when it closes while retaining completed per-account cache entries.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open any create/edit automation dialog with cloud automations enabled while leaving the workspace picker closed.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Dialog DOM and draft creation can proceed without all row checks, so the per-row REST burst is off the immediate render critical path. It competes with cloud refresh/tool loading and is only required if the user later opens the picker; selected-target validation remains legitimately required.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch repository metadata to inspect the private flag.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One GitHub REST getRepository call per uncached GitHub recent-workspace row; the default unified picker caps the visible list at 10, while legacy mode may expose additional fallback session workspaces.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Opening the automation dialog built workspace rows locally and issued no per-row repository visibility reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Not required for initial dialog rendering, but consumes interactive-priority network capacity and can delay cloud refresh/tool data or later picker readiness.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of uncached GitHub repository rows in recent/fallback workspaces after picker deduplication and the active list cap.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each uncached row queues independently through a shared Limiter(5): up to five repository REST requests run at once and the rest drain afterward. There is per-key caching but no batch API or deferral until picker open.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Repository eligibility is cached per workspace for the account-store lifetime, so a warm dialog reuses results; account/client changes and refresh clear the cache and trigger the hidden-row observer again. The finding concerns cold or invalidated caches. No negative retry loop occurs within an account lifetime.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: dialog construction installs the autorun, every row read reaches the cache-miss request path, and tests establish five-way concurrency.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact number of GitHub rows and network latency vary, but a full default recent list yields ten requests and the code-proven fan-out is independent of prevalence.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: the diff eagerly fans a hidden UI section into multiple network reads that are unnecessary for this scenario.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open, edit, or save a cloud automation and configure allowed tools.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opening an existing cloud dialog starts the catalog request asynchronously and does not block rendering or unchanged save. A new cloud definition that defaults to all catalog tools waits for the single catalog load on save, which is required to preserve the requested tool selection semantics.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load and parse the provider tool catalog.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One GET /automations/tools per cold account session after Cloud becomes selected.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No tool-catalog request or tool-selection UI existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off dialog-render critical path; on the save critical path only for a new cloud definition whose complete default tool set is not yet known.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Validate selected repository privacy and canonicalize the cloud workspace.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One repository metadata read for the selected uncached repository, potentially shared with the row cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Cloud target eligibility was not exposed in this dialog.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cloud target validity/save is gated on this result, as required by private-repository eligibility.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One account catalog plus one selected repository, not the number of tools during ordinary dialog rendering.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: At most one listTools request is active because loading and ready states suppress duplicates. Selected repository eligibility shares the five-wide limiter but is a single key in this scenario.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The Mission Control tool catalog is coalesced by loading/ready state and cached once per account session; failures become an explicit retryable error. Eligibility for the selected workspace reuses the same per-workspace cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: state guards prove one in-flight catalog request, and save only awaits it for the new-definition select-all case.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Catalog payload size and service latency are unknown, but request coalescing and account-lifetime caching bound the mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: the new calls are single-flight, cached, and either off the critical path or necessary to serialize the requested definition.

Scenarios.Scenario: Choose Work in GitHub, search for a private repository, and accept it.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Authentication and repository search occur only after the user chooses Work in GitHub. Selection then waits for one eligibility result before applying the target, so these boundaries are intentionally on the selection critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Authenticate for repository access and search known/recent GitHub repositories.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One authentication/access step on picker open, then at most one live repository-search request per debounced query.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The automation dialog had no Work in GitHub repository search.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required to populate the explicitly opened repository picker.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Verify the selected repository is private.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One metadata read for the selected repository unless already cached.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No cloud repository selection existed in this dialog.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Selection waits for private-repository verification before accepting the target.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of deliberate debounced search queries; one final selected repository.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: RepositoryPicker cancels the prior search when input changes, leaving one effective search at a time. The chosen repository contributes one eligibility request through the shared five-wide limiter.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Repository search results are not cached by this layer; in-flight searches are cancelled and input is debounced by 300 ms. The final repository eligibility result is cached per canonical workspace for the account lifetime.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the picker lifecycle, cancellation stores, debounce, and target cache are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Search service latency varies, but cancellation and debounce prevent concurrent query bursts.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: network work is user-initiated, serialized/cancelled, and necessary for the feature.

Scenarios.Scenario: Switch workspace or execution provider while editing an automation draft.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The diff now waits for outgoing draft capture before workspace/session-type selection is applied, preserving unsaved configuration. Agent-host configuration resolution can be asynchronous, but this ordering is intentional and bounded by cancellation/timeouts; the existing synchronizer also captures before retargeting its underlying draft.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Capture provider-owned draft configuration before changing execution target.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one provider configuration capture for the outgoing target during a user selection; agent-host resolution is generally the already-started draft config round trip.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Retarget synchronization captured configuration asynchronously after the picker event rather than gating application of the visible selection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The selection waits for capture so unsaved provider-owned state is not lost. The later synchronizer capture reads the now-resolved state and no second remote boundary was established.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One capture per deliberate workspace or session-type switch, serialized rather than collection-scaled.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Draft synchronization is sequenced by one syncPromise/generation; replacement cancels or invalidates stale work rather than running target transitions concurrently.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Draft configurations are retained by target key in the synchronizer. Provider configuration resolution may already be warm from eager draft initialization; subsequent capture copies the resolved state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the ordering change; lower for incremental boundary cost because draft config resolution was already eagerly started and pre-existing retarget synchronization also captured it.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Agent-host readiness latency varies and can approach the timeout, but no safe independent way to apply the target before authoritative capture was established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the wait enforces required ordering, is cancellable/serialized, and no avoidable additional expensive boundary was proven.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render automation cards/accessibility text and convert fixed UTC schedules for display.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Conversion runs synchronously while formatting each visible card/accessibility entry and once when opening/saving a dialog; it performs constant arithmetic and no external work.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of rendered automation cards or accessible-content entries.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous UI work, one constant-time conversion per rendered definition; no queue or boundary.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Schedule conversion has no cache and allocates one small projected schedule object only for UTC daily/weekly definitions.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: helper implementation is bounded arithmetic/object creation only.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Automation card counts vary, but the added work is constant and very small per item.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: linear constant-time formatting is appropriate and no expensive boundary or material allocation was introduced.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete 25-file inventory and the performance-sensitive dialog, store, picker, schedule, and provider paths. Submitted one medium-confidence/high-mechanism-confidence boundary-fanout finding for eager per-row repository REST checks while the picker is closed. Tool loading is single-flight/account-cached, repository search is user-initiated and cancelled, target capture is serialized for correctness, and schedule projection is constant-time.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
